chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) is forgiven for the extent of his voice, and everything that hears it testifies on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for the Mu'adhdhin who calls to prayer?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the Mu'adhdhin's role as a spiritual conduit, where the forgiveness granted corresponds to the reach of his voice and every listener becomes a witness to his devotion. This concept reflects the communal nature of worship in Islam, linking the individual act of calling to prayer with the collective testimony of the community on the Day of Judgment. It elevates the Mu'adhdhin from a mere announcer to a participant in the cosmic witness of faith.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Al Halby, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Muezzin, there would seek Forgiveness for him (everything) up to the extent of his voice, and there would testify for him everything which hears it’.
en.sarwar: 28. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al-Halabiy from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘

One who recites Adhan receives forgiveness for the sins as big as the space his voice fills and everything hearing him bears witness to this fact.’” (Ahadith 9-28 are best expressed in the form of fatwa.)
